chunks: 4980 - And in the narration of ʿAbdullāh ibn Maymūn, from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father عليه السلام, he said:
“Yaʿqūb said to his son Yūsuf عليه السلام: ‘O my son, do not commit fornication, for if a bird were to commit fornication, its feathers would scatter.’”

key_terms.الطَّيْرَ: The bird, used here as part of a striking moral comparison.
key_terms.لَا تَزْنِ: Do not commit fornication; a direct prohibition against zina.
key_terms.لَتَنَاثَرَ رِيشُهُ: Its feathers would scatter; an image showing disgrace and destructive consequence.

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith teach about the seriousness of zina?
ai.summary: This hadith conveys a moral warning from Prophet Yaʿqūb عليه السلام to Prophet Yūsuf عليه السلام against zina. It emphasizes the grave ugliness and destructive effect of the act by using a vivid image: if even a bird were to commit it, its feathers would fall away.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4980 - In the narration of Abdullah ibn Maymun from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) from his father, Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as), it is reported:
"Prophet Ya'qub (as) said to his son Yusuf (as): 'O' my son, do not commit fornication, for if a bird were to commit fornication, its feathers would fall off.'"
